correctness.summary: Under the source's contradiction hypothesis, its stated c0-sum closure sends any counterexample A to B=A⊕c0(I) for arbitrarily large I. Choosing |I|>|A| gives |B|>|A|, verifies the source order's non-absorption clause by cardinality, and makes B a strict successor. Hence counterexample types have unbounded cardinalities and admit no set-sized skeleton. The source's direct-sum upper bounds are set-indexed Banach algebras; ordinary Zorn's lemma cannot be applied to the resulting proper-class collection.

originality.scope: to the best of our knowledge
originality.summary: The source is a recent preprint whose central claim is presented as closing a known 2007 proof gap. Searches by identifier, title, amenability terminology, Zorn, cardinality, proper class, correction, and gap did not locate a public statement of this obstruction. Standard set/class and Zorn facts are prior art; novelty is limited to identifying and formalizing their consequence for this specific proof.

value.summary: The obstruction bears directly on the main theorem of a current functional-analysis preprint and shows that its cardinal-enlargement device defeats the maximal-element step needed by the proof. The same mechanism is reusable in other maximality arguments over Banach-algebra classes closed under arbitrarily large c0-sums.

limitations: The claimed amenability implication is not proved false.
No counterexample to the implication is constructed.
The finding concerns the proof in arXiv:2609.17428v1; an unrelated proof could exist.
